note: THE-346 fixes six defects the founder found on a phone. Five are geometry and one - Share on web - creates a PUBLIC LINK to a church's internal note, which is the only item here that can leak data, so it is answered first and by SHAPE rather than by a rule. NO firestore.rules CHANGE IS NEEDED AND NONE IS MADE: the share record lives at the top-level publicNotes/{token}, which has NO RULE and therefore no client read and no client write, and every access - minting, revoking and the signed-out reader's own fetch - goes through the Admin SDK in app/api/docs/public-share and app/n/[token]. That is THE-324's posture applied one ticket later, and it is why firestore.rules is byte-identical and this record carries NO rules digest: THE-333 and THE-341 each spelling one is what turned THE-325 red, twice, and THE-342 recorded that lesson. /docs/{docId}'s read is untouched - it is still isAuthenticated() AND (tenant admin OR createdBy OR sharedWith) - because widening it is the one change that would expose every note rather than the one being shared. THE URL IS NOT GUESSABLE: 32 bytes from node:crypto randomBytes, base64url, 43 characters, 256 bits, the same shape THE-324 chose; a Firestore auto-id was REJECTED because it is 20 characters with a timestamp prefix, so ids minted near each other sort near each other and sharing one note would put a minute's worth of notes in a searchable neighbourhood. The token is the DOCUMENT ID, not a field, so resolution is one get() by primary key - no query, no ordering, and firestore.indexes.json untouched, which matters because it does NOT deploy on merge (deploy-rules.yml runs firestore:rules,storage only) so an index added there is inert and the query throws failed-precondition in production. REVOKING ACTUALLY REVOKES, and it is proven by FETCHING AFTER REVOKE rather than by reading a flag: revokePublicNote DELETES the record, there is no active:false and no expiry for a later reader to forget, nothing of the note is copied into the share record so no stale copy can outlive the revocation, /n/[token] is force-dynamic so nothing is cached, and re-sharing mints a NEW token so a revoked link stays dead forever. The doc's own publicShare field is a MIRROR and is client-writable; planting one grants nothing, because the reader resolves the server-only record first. THE MEASUREMENTS ARE REAL: happy-dom has no layout engine, so every one of the six claims is measured in Chromium over CDP at 380/768/1024/1280/1440, and the menu is OPENED through the real component rather than replicated - #475 shipped 33 measured tests over a menu that never opened. TWO FINDINGS ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. First, the chat composer's width is NOT caused by AdminCommunity: AdminDashboard wraps the whole screen in p-4 for the conversation rail's sake and the thread adds px-4 of its own, so the pill spanned 316px of 380 - and the shell's padding is NOT removed, because the rail carries none of its own below lg and dropping it would push every channel row against the screen edge; the gutter is cancelled for the thread pane only. Second, TabsTrigger's transition-all animates min-height, so a suite that measures two animation frames after a viewport change reads a DRIFTING mid-flight value - 7.7469px then 1.43015px on consecutive runs - which is the same artefact THE-323's header records from the other side and attributes to timing rather than to the class; this ticket's measured page suppresses transitions and measures the resting layout. NO new token, component or dependency, and the lockfile THE-274 pins to an exact length is untouched.

entries.why: THE-346 owns this change and it is the notes editor's TOOLBAR and its MENU. The founder: "The 'export' button should be just the 3 dots." The labelled Export button and the triggerLabel prop that produced it are both GONE, so every caller gets the same three dots the tree's note cards already had. The menu itself was HAND-ROLLED - a relative div, an absolutely-positioned w-48 panel, plain buttons in place of menu items, and its own mousedown listener - and is the installed dropdown-menu primitive now, which is what brings Escape, focus return, roving focus, typeahead and menuitem roles that the hand-rolled version never had. Export is a DropdownMenuSub carrying PDF/DOCX/Markdown, the shape AttachMenu uses for its four category flyouts, which is what the founder asked for by name: "something like the paperclip from chat". Three rows are NEW - Share on web, Share to blog draft, and Share to Livestream, which MOVED here from the header bar per "we have to move the button from the headerbar into the more drawer" and is NOT duplicated there. handleShareToLivestream is byte-identical; only its trigger moved. The blog draft is written status:'draft' deliberately - a sermon note must not reach a church's public blog from one tap. The EXPAND toggle moved out of the right-hand group to sit immediately right of "Notes", measured rather than asserted from a class, and gained min-h-11/min-w-11 because p-1.5 around a 16px glyph is 27px and not a tap target. A second effect publishes setNavHidden from the SAME editorFullscreen state the header effect uses, with a cleanup, so the nav returns on all three exits - pressing expand again, leaving the note, and unmounting - which is the trap this ticket must not ship. The delete row's hardcoded text-red-600/bg-red-50 is gone in favour of the primitive's own destructive variant, so this file introduces no colour literal. NOTHING ELSE MOVED: every Firestore path, the save funnel, the share modal, the tree and the quick switcher are untouched.

THE-346 owns this change and it is ONE wrapper and one piece of state. The founder: "On phone if I press on expand the bottom nav menu should disappear as well, and reappear when I exit the notes or press the button again." navHidden joins headerHidden in the shared header API, and the nav is hidden by a WRAPPER carrying max-lg:hidden lg:contents rather than by interpolating the flag into the nav's own className - and that shape is load-bearing, not stylistic. FOUR other measured suites (THE-279, THE-286, THE-296, THE-337) DISCOVER this nav out of this file by matching data-nav-shell followed by a plain double-quoted class string, precisely so a nav that moved cannot leave them measuring a stale hand copy. The first attempt interpolated the flag, turned that attribute into a template literal, and all four stopped finding it - loudly, which is what a discovery guard is for. So the nav's own class string is BYTE-IDENTICAL and the conditional lives one element up. display:contents makes the wrapper transparent to layout, so the fixed bottom nav still positions against the viewport and the desktop rail keeps its place in the shell's flex row. The two states sit in DIFFERENT media queries - max-lg:hidden below lg, lg:contents above - so neither has to out-specify the other, and the desktop rail survives a phone's expand toggle. It is display rather than a z-index because the editor is an ordinary in-flow screen with no stacking context to raise, and a competing z-index would leave the nav painted under it while still taking its 65px and still swallowing taps in that band. Nothing else in this file moved: no nav array, no route, no tab.

THE-346 owns this change and it is ONE field on the shared header API - setNavHidden - plus its default and its doc comment. It is a SEPARATE switch from setHeaderHidden even though AdminDocs today drives both from the same focusMode && !!openDoc, and the comment says so plainly rather than inventing a difference: an earlier draft of this ticket claimed the header was hidden merely on opening a note, the mounted test disproved it, and the prose was corrected instead of the test. They stay two switches because they hide two different elements and neither could hide the other - headerHidden toggles a wrapper that is already lg:hidden, so plain hidden is enough, while the nav is ONE element that is the fixed bottom nav below lg and the relative 64px side rail above it, so its hide must be breakpoint-scoped or a phone's expand toggle would strip the desktop rail. The comment also states the contract that keeps this from becoming a trap: the caller must restore it on exit AND on unmount. Nothing else in the file changed - AdminScreenHeader itself renders identically.

THE-346 owns this change and it is ONE className token: -mx-4 lg:mx-0 on the thread pane, plus the note explaining it. The founder: "the input text field is not wide enough to the whole width of the screen." MEASURED at 380px before the fix, the composer's pill spanned 316px of 380 - 32px of gutter each side - because TWO paddings stack, and THE CAUSE IS NOT IN THIS FILE: AdminDashboard wraps the whole community screen in p-4 pb-0 lg:p-0 and ChannelThread/DmThread then add px-4 of their own around the composer. The message list above reads as edge-to-edge because its content is box-less bubbles hugging the right, while the composer draws a bordered bg-surface-tint pill, so the same 32px shows up as dead space either side of a visible box. THE SHELL'S p-4 IS DELIBERATELY NOT REMOVED, and that was the first thing tried: the left rail - channels, Admin DMs, Member DMs - carries NO horizontal padding of its own below lg, only lg:px-4, so the shell's gutter is what keeps those rows off the screen edge, and dropping it would have fixed the composer and broken a screen the founder did not complain about. So the gutter is cancelled for the THREAD PANE only, which below lg is a full-width takeover anyway; -mx-4 fills the parent's padding box and never leaves its border box, so the shell's overflow-hidden has nothing to clip, and from lg up the pane is a bordered card in a row and the margin goes back to 0. After: pill 16 -> 364 at 380px, the same 16px inset the bubbles sit on. No read, no write, no handler and no import moved.

THE-346 owns this change and it is THREE className strings on the List/Month tab bar. The founder: "look at how the buttons for list and month look like. It needs to be fixed." MEASURED in Chromium at 380px: TabsList 32.00px tall (y 0 -> 32), TabsTrigger 44.00px (y 3.5 -> 47.5) - the pill is TALLER THAN THE BOX IT LIVES IN and hangs 6px at each end out of the bottom of it, which is the "floating, misaligned" the founder is describing seen from the other side. Both numbers are correct in isolation and that is the trap: ui/tabs.tsx fixes the list at h-8 through group-data-[orientation=horizontal]/tabs:h-8, which is the right desktop density and is shared by every other Tabs in the app, and THE-308 put a required 44px tap floor on the triggers. Nobody raised the list to hold them, and THE-308's own measured suite could not see it because it measured the TRIGGERS and never the relationship. PR 482's class of fault was RULED OUT rather than assumed away: the compiled stylesheet carries exactly one non-utility min-height rule (::-webkit-date-and-time-value) and the 32/44 split reproduces with these two triggers and nothing else on the page, so it is local styling and no injected global. The list is RELEASED to h-auto below sm rather than given a number - it wraps whatever the triggers need, 50px today - and the sm: half restores the primitive's 32px above, where Rule 4 owns density; hard-coding h-[50px] would be the same mistake one breakpoint along. The variant is spelled in full on both halves because a plain h-auto loses on specificity to the primitive's two-selector variant whatever cn() does. min-h-[44px] was NOT inert and is respelled min-h-11 only because that is the same 44px off the spacing scale; this file now mints no raw pixel height at all. ui/tabs.tsx is NOT edited and its digest is untouched. THE-345's price gating and THE-308's lazy month-view mount are byte-identical, and no Firestore path moved.

THE-346 owns this change and it is ONE className - pl-12, removed - plus the note explaining it. The founder: "In news user app when creating a post put that paperclip and pin button in the left to be in parallel with the user profile picture." The composer's text row is flex items-start gap-3 with a w-9 (36px) avatar, so the textarea starts at 48px, and pl-12 is exactly that. It is CORRECT on the four rows above - poll options, attachment chips, the image strip and the embed card all continue the sentence the textarea started - and wrong on this one, which is the composer's action bar and belongs to the whole composer rather than to the text column. Measured at 380px before: the paperclip's glyph sat at x=64 against an avatar at x=16; after, both at x=16, at all five widths. The paperclip's -ml-2 STAYS, and it is why this is pl-0 rather than pl-2: that negative margin exists so the GLYPH aligns rather than the 44px hit area around it, which is the edge the founder is pointing at. THE-345's two eventPriceLabel spans, its import, the feed reads, the embed cards and every other byte are untouched.

THE-346 owns this change and it is TWO FAULTS, both fixed, with #476's and THE-342's work untouched. The founder: "In map I should not be able to zoom out this much", with a screenshot showing the world repeating THREE TIMES across and grey void above and below. Those are not one bug seen twice. (1) NOTHING SET A FLOOR ON ZOOM - zoom={2} is only where the map STARTS, and Leaflet let you scroll out to 0 where the whole world is 256px and the rest of the container is the void behind the tile pane; minZoom={2} is the declared floor, and it is RAISED at run time to whatever fits the container via Leaflet's own getBoundsZoom, because 256*2^2 = 1024px of world covers a 380px phone four times over and falls 416px short of 1440 - a width-adaptive floor is what answers the brief's warning that width is not monotonic without a table of magic numbers. It only ever raises (Math.max against 2), it walks the CURRENT view up when the floor rises above it, it re-applies on resize, and a non-finite answer is ignored. (2) NOTHING STOPPED THE WORLD REPEATING - Web Mercator tiles wrap in x by default, so past 256*2^z the same tiles are re-requested for the next copy and the same church is drawn in each one. noWrap on the TileLayer is the lever; worldCopyJump is NOT and is deliberately not set, because it changes what panning does across the seam rather than whether the seam exists - setting it would have looked like a fix and changed nothing. maxBounds + maxBoundsViscosity keep the single world put once zoom can no longer reach the void, and the bounds are +/-85.05112878 rather than +/-90 because Web Mercator is cut at the latitude that makes the world square and that is the edge tiles exist up to; +/-90 would make getBoundsZoom answer one step too low, which is the void again. #476 IS UNTOUCHED: key={mapTheme} still remounts the TileLayer (react-leaflet builds L.TileLayer once on mount and does not re-issue tiles when url changes), the tile url is byte-identical, the OSM attribution string is byte-identical and attributionControl is still not false, and harvest-tiles-dark is unchanged. THE-342 IS UNTOUCHED and was CHECKED rather than assumed: the bounded read is by radius and never consults zoom or bounds, so a zoom floor changes what is drawn and not what is fetched. The gold and blue divIcon markers keep their pre-existing literals - marker colour is a palette change, not a zoom fix - and the four emoji an earlier draft wrote into this file's comments were removed, because the-333 and THE-342 sweep this file's raw source for them.

THE-346 owns this append and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-345 owned the one before it and THE-342 the one before that. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 63 -> 64 and this ticket's guard suite is added to RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-345's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired, and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-346 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere: it changes no rule, and THE-333 and THE-341 each spelling one is what turned THE-325 red both times, so this suite asks rulesDigestFailure() like every other pinner. The one item in this ticket that could have needed a rule - "Share on web", which creates a PUBLIC link to a church's internal note - needed none because the share record lives at the top-level publicNotes/{token}, which has NO rule and therefore no client access, and every path to it goes through the Admin SDK in a route. /docs/{docId}'s read is untouched.
